items.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023
items.q: I wound up adapting two pieces of William Walton that bore no relevance to each other

ctx.x: Did you ever get carried away with, you’re working on a 30-second spot and you write something that you really like and you start adding and expanding and then an alarm goes off and it says all right, remember your task here, maybe set this aside and make something out of it later?

Not so much that, but I did write things that almost got thrown away on — I remember I wrote one thing for a week-long campaign for a national newspaper. It was a special campaign. And I always really liked it. So when I got to score a silent movie for the London Film Festival, years later, I dredged it up and used it in that. You know so more that. I mean I was always focused on the task in hand. In fact there was one commercial I got to shadow, they hired Sir Michael Tippitt to compose but they asked me to be…
Do you get residuals or payments after the fact for any of this kind of work?
